title: Phase 3 hardening: dual-signal indexer self-recognition (dir + prompt), loud mismatch incident
description: cc-recall-hie's fix (PR #68) made isIndexerTranscript's prompt-signature check work again, but left it as the SOLE signal -- a text heuristic over data that already proved it can be silently transformed upstream once. runClaudeHeadless always pins cwd: INDEXER_CWD, so every future indexer run is structurally guaranteed to land under INDEXER_PROJECT_DIR -- a fact, not a heuristic. listTranscripts already uses this for backfill exclusion; indexSession's forward-capture path deliberately doesn't (historical stray transcripts predate the dedicated cwd). Add the directory check as a second independent signal alongside the prompt check in indexSession: either recognizing it is enough to skip (keeps historical-stray coverage), and disagreement between the two (dir says indexer, prompt heuristic doesn't, or vice versa) logs a distinct loud incident -- the concrete tripwire that would have caught cc-recall-hie's exact failure mode on day one, independent of whether anyone notices the spawn-rate side effect or the watchdog happens to be running.
acceptance_criteria: indexSession recognizes an indexer transcript via EITHER dir match (project === INDEXER_PROJECT_DIR) OR prompt-signature match. A mismatch between the two signals logs a new incident kind (e.g. indexer_recognition_mismatch) via the existing logIncident primitive. TDD: failing tests first for (a) dir-only match with a prompt that wouldn't match, (b) prompt-only match outside the dir (historical stray, existing coverage preserved), (c) mismatch logs the new incident kind. All existing tests still pass.
close_reason: Merged d7353e4 (PR #72). isIndexerRun() in src/engine.ts now checks both directory match (structurally guaranteed for all future indexer runs) and prompt-signature match; disagreement logs a loud indexer_recognition_mismatch incident. This is the deeper Phase 3 tripwire, not just the shallower doctor liveness check from cc-recall-13a.

title: [bug] Indexer's own headless sessions re-enter enrichment path, no self-exclusion guard exists
description: Live on deployed 0.2.1: 374/435 (86%) of sidecar session writes over the last ~45h are cc-recall's own indexer project (-Users-joe--claude-cc-recall-indexer), vs 61 from real work. Enrichment spawn-rate ceiling (30/60min) saturated across 13 separate hourly windows, 60 spawn_ceiling_paused incidents logged over 2 days -- not a single burst. No backfill process running to explain it. hooks/session-end.mjs spawns 'cc-recall index' unconditionally on every SessionEnd with zero project-based exclusion; grep of src/ and bin/ found no guard anywhere preventing the indexer's own headless claude -p sessions from re-entering the enrichment path. Only the blunt spawn-rate ceiling bounds it -- and it's being hit constantly rather than staying idle. Same root-cause family as Incident B (headless subprocess's SessionEnd hook re-triggering more spawns) but Phase 1's fix apparently only addressed corpus-convergence, not forward-capture self-triggering. Separately, ops/cc-recall-watchdog (built in Phase 3 specifically to catch this independently) is not installed -- launchctl list shows only claude-mem's two watchdog jobs, not com.ccrecall.watchdog-light.
acceptance_criteria: Root cause identified via systematic-debugging (red test reproducing the self-trigger before fix). Guard added so the indexer's own forward-capture sessions do not re-enter full LLM enrichment. cc-recall-watchdog launchd job installed and confirmed running. sidecar session growth over a subsequent multi-hour window is proportional to real usage (indexer-project share drops to a small minority).
notes: Two Phase 3 hardening passes landed: cc-recall-13a/PR#70 (doctor watchdog-installed check, shallower -- merged bcd3a30) and cc-recall-4fc/PR#72 (dual-signal indexer self-recognition + loud mismatch incident, the actual tripwire for a recurrence of this exact bug class -- merged d7353e4). Phase 6 spec updated with Guard-fixture realism + Self-verification requirements. Both PM-001 and PM-003 postmortems corrected. Neither #70 nor #72 has been released yet (main only, v0.2.2 still deployed) -- same merged-vs-deployed gap PM-003 named, lower stakes here since both are hardening/detection, not behavioral fixes. Original live-verification window (restart, use normally, re-check session-end.log + doctor) still pending.
close_reason: Verified live post-restart: dual-signal self-recognition guard working (indexer-run share of session-end.log entries dropped from reported 86% to ~1.9%, all correctly skipped not re-enriched); com.ccrecall.watchdog-light installed and running (launchctl LastExitStatus 0, ticking every 5min); watchdog state circuit breakers (cb_spawn_rate, cb_sidecar_growth) both idle at 0, no pending/open incidents. 0.3.0 (incl. PR #70/#72) confirmed deployed to plugin cache.

title: Phase 1: root-cause and fix Incident B (hook-triggered runaway re-indexing)
description: The live P0 blocking cc-recall (README banner, commit 70c2ca0): SessionEnd/UserPromptSubmit hooks trigger duplicate indexing sub-agent sessions seconds apart, burning quota. Recurred 6 days after Incident A's fix (c0713ca/f0190fd) with no source changes on main in between -- root cause is NOT diagnosed anywhere yet.
design: Leading hypothesis: a headless claude -p enrichment session is itself a full CC session subject to the caller's global hooks (cwd is pinned to INDEXER_CWD but --setting-sources is not, since overriding it breaks auth). Its own SessionEnd fires cc-recall index against its own transcript -- isIndexerTranscript should skip it cheaply but each occurrence is still a real subprocess spawn seconds apart. Corroborating evidence: 206 temp_github_* throwaway plugin-cache checkouts dated continuously 2026-07-31 through 2026-08-06, consistent with abnormal session-start volume. Alternative/compounding theory: ensure-built.sh only rebuilds dist/ if missing and swallows build failures (cc-recall-vfn), so a stale pre-fix build may have kept running in the installed plugin cache. Steps: (1) confirm which dist/ was actually running in ~/.claude/plugins/cache/agent-marketplace/cc-recall during 08-01..08-06; (2) reproduce nested-hook-firing directly with a headless claude -p and the plugin installed, CC_RECALL_LLM on/off; (3) check hooks/session-end.mjs for any concurrency guard (currently none); (4) fix at the confirmed layer: idempotency lock keyed by transcript path+hash in indexSession/CLI entry, and/or force CC_RECALL_LLM=0 for cc-recall's own claude -p subprocesses, and/or fix cc-recall-vfn for real + clean the temp_github_* accumulation.
acceptance_criteria: Root cause confirmed via reproduction (not just hypothesis). Regression test is red on pre-fix code (verified by stashing the fix) and green after. A bounded real session triggers SessionEnd and produces exactly one indexing attempt, verified via session-end.log.
notes:
ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED (2026-08-10, via direct evidence, not hypothesis):

The installed plugin cache at ~/.claude/plugins/cache/agent-marketplace/cc-recall/0.1.0/ is a git
checkout PINNED AT COMMIT 1bc6ec1 (2026-06-16) -- six weeks before Incident A was even discovered
(~2026-07-29). Its dist/bin/cc-recall.js was last built 2026-06-26T22:09 (ensure-built.sh only
builds once, on first run, iff the file is missing -- confirmed by reading the script, it has
NO staleness/version check). grep for isIndexerTranscript/INDEXER_CWD/claude-haiku in that
cache's SOURCE (not just dist) returns nothing -- the cache was never re-synced at all, not just
never rebuilt.

Why it was never re-synced: package.json "version" is 0.1.0 in BOTH the live cache and current
main -- the 0.2.0 release-please bump never merged to main (still sitting on branch
release-please--branches--main--components--cc-recall). Claude Code's plugin cache is keyed by
version string (.../cc-recall/<version>/); since the version string never changed, the installer
had no signal to fetch anything new.

CONCLUSION: Incident B is NOT a new/different bug from Incident A. It is Incident A's exact
mechanism (bare claude -p inheriting the interactive Opus model + caller's cwd, no
isIndexerTranscript guard because that guard did not exist yet in this checkout), continuing to
run completely unpatched in production for 6+ weeks, because c0713ca/f0190fd were merged to
GitHub main but NEVER ACTUALLY DEPLOYED -- 'fixed on GitHub' != 'fixed in the running system'.
The README P0 banner (70c2ca0, Aug 6) is not describing a recurrence of a fixed bug; it's the
first time anyone noticed the original bug never stopped.

Secondary, confirmed-but-not-primary finding: empirically verified (isolated scratch-dir repro,
not the disabled cc-recall plugin itself) that a headless  subprocess DOES fire the
caller's configured SessionEnd hook on normal completion (not just SIGTERM, which is the only
case Claude Code's own docs cover) -- and there is no documented Claude-Code-level
nesting-detection, so a plugin that spawns claude -p must guard against its own hooks
re-triggering it. In current (already-fixed, unmerged-to-production) main-branch code this is
correctly caught by isIndexerTranscript before any LLM call, so it is defense-in-depth for Phase
3, not Incident B's root cause.

Actual fix needed for Phase 1, in priority order:
1. ensure-built.sh: rebuild when source changes, not just when dist/ is missing (currently: zero
   staleness detection, builds exactly once per cache directory, ever).
2. Cut a real version bump so the fix actually deploys (a version-identical package.json means
   Claude Code's version-keyed plugin cache never re-fetches, independent of #1).
3. For the user's own current install: force-clear/rebuild the stale 0.1.0 cache directory now,
   don't wait for the next natural install cycle.
4. (Defense-in-depth, Phase 3, not blocking) idempotency guard against nested SessionEnd
   self-firing for cc-recall's own claude -p subprocesses.
fix/transcript-write-safety branch content confirmed byte-for-byte identical to main (already merged via squash f0190fd/#55). Left in place -- Safety Net correctly blocked a force-delete since squash merges break git's ancestry check. Recommend Joe delete manually at his convenience; not a blocker.
close_reason: Merged: PR #57 (d0c9914). Root cause confirmed (stale plugin cache, never rebuilt due to ensure-built.sh checking existence not staleness, compounded by never-bumped package.json version). Fixed with content-hash staleness detection, defensive shasum guard, file-identity hashing. 4 rounds of review, all real findings fixed, all false positives documented and declined with evidence.

title: C3: read-modify-rename races Claude Code appender; orphaned inode loses live writes
description:
src/surfaces/transcript-writer.ts:142 (read) -> :116-120 (atomicWrite = writeFileSync tmp + renameSync).

Three problems: (a) anything Claude Code appends between read and rename is discarded, and synthesis sits inside that window (up to LLM_TIMEOUT_MS=60s); (b) renameSync replaces the inode, so a live session holding an append fd writes to an unlinked file forever, silently; (c) no fsync on tmp fd before rename, none on the directory after — power loss can land a zero-length transcript, which C2 then makes worse.

Fix: skip transcripts with recent mtime / current CLAUDE_SESSION_ID; re-read and compare source hash immediately before write; fsync fd and dir.
close_reason: Merged: PR #60 (7c8c483). Fixed the renameSync inode-swap race for live sessions with a two-signal liveness guard (CLAUDE_SESSION_ID match + mtime recency), scoped to non-forward provenance so ordinary SessionEnd writes are never affected, and exempted for content cc-recall already wrote (so --force repair passes aren't self-defeated by their own prior write's fresh mtime). 3 rounds of review, 4 real bugs found and fixed (2 in the original implementation, 2 in the first review-fix pass), all verified with red/green regression tests. Filed cc-recall-m32 as a genuine but pre-existing follow-up (sidecar upsert ordering) found during review.

title: C1: unhandled rejection at CLI entrypoint kills process on any per-file error
description:
bin/cc-recall.ts:113 (runIndex) and :316 (await program.parseAsync). runIndex calls indexSession with no try, and the top-level await has no catch. Any throw — starting with readFileSync at src/engine.ts:68 — becomes an unhandled rejection that aborts the process.

Confirmed 13,052 times in ~/.claude/cc-recall/logs/session-end.log (ENOENT on moved/deleted transcripts).

NOTE: enumeration (listTranscripts/transcriptsInDir) is correctly guarded and backfillOne try/catch is complete — the escape is specifically the CLI path that /recall:backfill and the SessionEnd hook both shell out to.

Fix: existsSync guard in runIndex + try/catch around parseAsync + process.on(unhandledRejection).
notes:
PARTIALLY fixed on main by PR #55 (f0190fd) — NOT closing.

Landed: runIndex now guards with existsSync before reading (bin/cc-recall.ts:117), and the
top-level `await program.parseAsync` is wrapped in try/catch so a rejection becomes a one-line
message and exit 1 rather than a raw V8 stack dump. That covers the ENOENT crash-loop this bead
was opened for (13,052 occurrences in session-end.log).

Still missing: the process.on('unhandledRejection') net this bead also asks for. Verified absent
on origin/main — `grep -c unhandledRejection` returns 0. Without it, any rejection originating
outside the parseAsync await (a detached promise, a late-settling handle) still aborts silently.

That is a ~5-line addition and belongs in the next cc-recall PR alongside the retention work.
COMPLETED on branch fix/retention-and-rotation (151192d) — not yet merged.

The remaining piece is in: process.on('unhandledRejection') at the CLI entrypoint, logging the
reason (with stack when it is an Error) and setting exitCode 1. It does not swallow — exit stays
non-zero — it only makes the reason attributable, which is the difference between a diagnosable
line and the 13,052 mystery entries this bead was opened for.

With #55's existsSync guard and parseAsync try/catch already on main, all three parts of the
original fix are now present. Close this once the branch merges.
close_reason: Merged: PR #58 (aca1b34), landing fix/retention-and-rotation. Reviewed and fixed further in the process (createClaudeMemGate no longer overrides explicit caller options, --only-heuristic works without requiring --force).

title: C2: revert/auto-restore writes a stale snapshot over live transcript content
description:
src/surfaces/transcript-writer.ts:110-114 (ensureBackup returns early if backup exists — written ONCE, never refreshed), :155 (auto-restore), :169 (didRevertTranscript).

Failure: session indexed at 400 lines; resumed weeks later, grows to 1900; SessionEnd re-indexes; integrity check fails for any reason; restore copies the 400-line snapshot back. 1500 lines of conversation lost, and the thrown error says "restored from backup" as if that were safe.

Violates the AGENTS.md "reversible" property. Fix: back up per write (versioned/content-hash suffix), never restore a snapshot older than the read at :142.
notes:
FIXED and verified on main by PR #55 (f0190fd).

The auto-restore path no longer restores the first-ever backup. writeRecordToTranscript and
didRevertTranscript both take a takePreWriteSnapshot() of the file as it exists for THIS write
and restore from that, so a resumed session that has grown since first indexing cannot be rolled
back to its first-indexed state. Verified present on origin/main.

Covered by tests: "a failed write leaves no .prewrite snapshot behind, and rolls the content
back" asserts both cleanup and that the restored content equals the pre-write bytes, and
"revert preserves turns appended since indexing" pins the growth case directly.
close_reason: Closed

title: H5: SessionStart build failure swallowed, producing 4,897 silent crash-loops
description:
hooks/ensure-built.sh:19-20 discards stdout, stderr, AND exit code of both pnpm install and pnpm build (|| true), then reports success. Every subsequent SessionEnd spawns a dist/bin/cc-recall.js that does not exist.

4,897 "Cannot find module .../dist/bin/cc-recall.js" in the log. Forward capture was dead for that entire period and nothing surfaced.

Fix: capture output; on failure return {"continue":true,"systemMessage":"cc-recall: build failed, forward capture disabled: ..."}. At minimum guard the spawn in session-end.mjs:57 with existsSync so you get one clear message instead of 4,897 stack traces.
notes:
FIXED on branch fix/retention-and-rotation (8c18081) — not yet merged; PR held until the

title: H3: no retry/backoff/concurrency/ceiling — a 429 makes the backfill loop run FASTER
description:
src/engine.ts:188 is a bare sequential for-await. Zero retry/backoff/throttle primitives in src/.

Worst property: rate-limit responses are invisible AND self-accelerating. runClaudeHeadless rejects on non-zero exit, synthesize catches and immediately proceeds. Failing calls return in ms vs ~15s for success, so a 429 storm makes the run finish FAST with a fully-degraded index, reporting "56037 processed, 56037 written, 0 failed" — because summary.failed only counts throws from indexSession and LLM failure never throws.

Also: no spend ceiling. --limit caps files, not LLM calls.

Fix: retry with jittered backoff on transient errors; consecutive-failure circuit breaker aborting past a threshold; --max-llm-calls. The breaker is what would have bounded the original incident regardless of root cause.
notes:
FIXED on branch fix/retention-and-rotation (aa772a7) — not yet merged; PR held for the ai-review bot work.

H3: breaker+ceiling+enriched/degraded reporting

Gates green: tsc/biome/eslint/vitest all 0, 83 tests. Four new tests cover the degradation path, including that intermittent failures must NOT trip the breaker (a success resets the counter).

title: H2: enrichment failure is unrecorded, making 8,673 sessions unrepairable except at full cost
description:
src/record/synthesizer.ts:346-350 returns the heuristic base on LLM failure — byte-identical in shape to a successful enrichment. No field distinguishes them; provenance only encodes forward/backfill/manual.

8,673 "LLM synthesis failed" lines already in the log. Those sessions have titles that are just a truncated first prompt — the exact low-quality state the project exists to fix — and no query can find them. Only remedy is backfill --force over all 56,037.

This is the cost incident in another form: the only available repair is the maximally expensive one.

Fix: add enrichment: llm|heuristic (+ enrichment_error) to recallRecordSchema, index it, add backfill --only-heuristic. Turns a 56,037-call repair into an 8,673-call one.
notes: FIXED on fix/retention-and-rotation — enrichment/enrichment_error on the record schema, --no-llm marked heuristic, and backfill --only-heuristic skipping enriched sessions before synthesis rather than after. Test asserts the cost directly: one enriched + one degraded session yields exactly one LLM call on the repair pass. Gates green, 86 tests.

title: H1: four unbounded write sinks, 5.1GB and growing, zero cleanup anywhere
description:
Grep-confirmed: no prune/rotate/unlink/maxAge/retention logic in src/, bin/, or hooks/. Measured live:
- backups/ 4.4GB / 40,156 files (transcript-writer.ts:113) — one full copy per indexed transcript, forever
- migrate-backups/ 577MB / 11,591 files (home-path.ts:160)
- logs/session-end.log 23MB / 309,548 lines (hooks/session-end.mjs:56, append, never rotated)
- index.db 96MB, never VACUUMed
- migrate-manifest.json 11MB, rewritten wholesale

~/.claude/projects is 12GB / 56,037 transcripts and only 40,156 are backed up — a completed backfill makes backups/ a byte-for-byte 12GB duplicate that never shrinks. 24GB of home dir for an index.

Fix: store the reversal diff (classify() already yields exactly the two injected lines) plus source hash, not a full copy. Add --retain-days. Rotate the log at ~10MB. VACUUM in doctor.
notes:
Re-measured 2026-07-31 07:5x, after PR #55 work:
  backups/            4.5G / 40,436 files  (was 4.4G / 40,156 — still growing)
  migrate-backups/    577M / 11,591 files
  logs/session-end.log 23M
  index.db            112M  (was 96M)
  migrate-manifest.json 11M
  ~/.claude/projects   12G / transcript corpus
Grep re-confirmed: zero retain/prune/rotate/maxAge/unlinkSync retention logic in src, bin, or hooks.

SAFETY BOUNDARY for whoever implements this: deleting accumulated backups is a data-loss-class
action and must not be done autonomously. The implementation should ship the retention *mechanism*
defaulting to dry-run — report what would be removed and how much it would reclaim — and leave the
actual prune to an explicit human-run invocation. Reclaiming 5GB is not urgent; deleting the wrong
5GB is unrecoverable.

Implementation shape per the original spec, in ascending risk:
 1. Rotate session-end.log at ~10MB (pure win, no data of value lost).
 2. VACUUM index.db in  (reclaims the 112M -> much smaller; rebuildable from transcripts).
 3. --retain-days on backups/ and migrate-backups/, dry-run by default.
 4. Store the reversal diff + source hash instead of a full copy. classify() already yields exactly
    the injected lines, so the reversal payload is two lines rather than a whole transcript. This is
    the change that stops the growth rather than managing it — and it is the one that needs the most
    care, since it changes the recovery contract for every future write.
Correction to the previous note: step 2 reads "VACUUM index.db in " — the target was the
`doctor` subcommand. Backticks in the note body were command-substituted by the shell and
that word was eaten. Full step 2: VACUUM index.db as part of `cc-recall doctor`.
MEASURED CORRECTION 2026-07-31: the index.db item in this bead is wrong.

Ran VACUUM against a copy of the live database (branch fix/retention-and-rotation, f1c18d5):
  before 96.5MB -> after 96.3MB, reclaimed 0.2MB, all 40,436 records still readable.

The sidecar is densely packed with real data, not carrying reclaimable slack. "never VACUUMed"
was true but the implied payoff is ~0. VACUUM is still shipped in `doctor` because it becomes
meaningful once retention pruning starts deleting rows, and because reporting the real number
beats leaving an untested assumption in place — but nobody should expect GBs from it.

The 5GB is backups/ (4.5G) and migrate-backups/ (577M). Those are the whole problem.

SHIPPED on fix/retention-and-rotation (branch pushed, PR not yet opened — waiting on #55 to
merge per lowest-number-first):
  - session-end.log rotation at 10MB, one generation kept, fully swallow-on-error since it runs
    inside a SessionEnd hook.
  - sidecar.vacuum() + doctor reporting.

STILL TO DO, in ascending risk:
  - --retain-days over backups/ and migrate-backups/, DRY-RUN BY DEFAULT. Report what would be
    removed and how much it reclaims; never delete without an explicit human-run invocation.
  - Store the reversal diff + source hash instead of a full transcript copy. classify() already
    yields exactly the injected lines, so the payload is two lines rather than a whole file. This
    is the change that stops the growth instead of managing it, and it alters the recovery
    contract for every future write — it needs its own review pass.

title: C4: mid-loop migrate failure leaves 29k file moves permanently unrevertible
description:
src/migrate/home-path.ts:178 (destructive moves applied first) vs :187-190 (manifest written only after ALL rewrites succeed). revertHomePaths (:219) throws without the manifest.

Live manifest on this machine: 33 dirMoves, 29505 fileMerges, 11591 rewrites. A throw at rewrite 6000 leaves the corpus half-migrated with no automated way back.

Also: :189 overwrites the manifest on every apply (second run destroys first run revert data, 11MB non-atomic write); :158 keys rewrite backups by basename in one flat dir while :99-100 explicitly models cross-dir filename collisions — on collision restoreRewrites writes the wrong session bytes.

Fix: incremental JSONL journal written as each op completes; per-file try/catch; namespace backups by dir-slug.

title: release-please auto-commits reformat package.json, fighting Biome's array-collapse and breaking CI on every release PR
description: release-please's generic JSON updater re-serializes package.json wholesale on every version-bump PR, always multi-lining short arrays (e.g. lint-staged's "*.ts": [...]). Biome's JSON formatter collapses that same array onto one line (fits within lineWidth). The two disagree every single release cycle: PR #76 (0.4.0) shipped the multi-line form and broke main's CI biome check; #78 fixed it by collapsing back to one line; PR #79 (0.4.1, auto-opened by release-please) already reintroduces the multi-line form in its diff. Merging #79 as-is will break CI again.
notes: Root cause confirmed 2026-08-17 while shipping 0.4.0/0.4.1 to unblock cc-recall-yhp's real-usage verification window. Candidate fixes not yet evaluated in depth: (a) add a biome-format step to the release-please GitHub Actions workflow that runs after release-please writes its PR branch, before CI evaluates it; (b) set Biome's json formatter expand mode to 'always' repo-wide to match release-please's style (touches every JSON file, a real style change, not just this one array); (c) exclude package.json from Biome's format enforcement (loses format consistency on that file going forward). Did not merge PR #79 (0.4.1) — merging as-is reintroduces the break; will need this fixed first, or the array manually re-collapsed again before merge.

title: Sidecar upsert happens before transcript write, so a skipped write can't be retried
description: engine.ts indexSession: sidecar.upsert(record, sourceHash) runs before writeToTranscript. If the transcript write is then skipped (stale-source, or the new active-session from cc-recall-kg8), the sidecar already has the new sourceHash stamped, so the next ordinary pass's !options.force && sidecar.getSourceHash(...) === sourceHash check treats it as unchanged and never retries the transcript write. Pre-existing for stale-source; the active-session skip path makes it more likely to actually occur since a live/recently-touched session is exactly the kind of file backfill sweeps repeatedly. Fix needs a design decision: don't upsert until the transcript write succeeds, or track a separate pending-transcript-write flag; not a one-line change, deferred.
notes: Ref: PR #60 review, comment 3755289647.

title: H4: claude-mem G0 health probe runs per record — 112k HTTP calls, up to 93h of pure timeout
description:
src/engine.ts:102 calls upsertToClaudeMem without skipG0, so every session pays verifyClaudeMemG0 = /api/health + /api/search (claude-mem.ts:60, :103), each with a 3s AbortSignal.timeout.

Over 56,037 transcripts: 112,074 HTTP round-trips to check one local daemon. With the worker down, each session burns up to 6s of pure timeout — a full backfill spends up to 93 hours waiting on a service that is off. 2,911 G0 failures already logged.

Fix: verify once in backfill() before the loop, pass skipG0 per record, re-probe on a TTL or after N consecutive failures.

title: backfill --max-llm-calls=0 aborts before processing any file, instead of degrading to heuristic-only
description: anthropicreviewbot (PR #58 review): createLlmBudget's stopReason() check runs at the top of the loop before any file is processed. For maxLlmCalls=0, calls(0)>=maxLlmCalls(0) is true on the very first iteration, so summary.abortedReason is set and summary.processed stays 0 -- the whole backfill aborts rather than processing every file heuristic-only (which is arguably the more useful interpretation of 'zero LLM calls allowed', and is already achievable via the separate llm:false/--no-llm mechanism). Needs a design decision on whether hitting the ceiling should abort the run (current, deliberate circuit-breaker behavior per summary.abortedReason) or degrade the remaining files to heuristic -- not a one-line fix, deferred rather than redesigning control flow under review-loop time pressure.
notes: Ref: PR #58 review threads, comments 3755059141 (early dup), 3755059150, 3755059135 (disputed, see reply).

title: Sidecar.vacuum() measurement is imprecise (page-count-based, in-memory no-op, TOCTOU)
description: anthropicreviewbot (PR #58 review) flagged three related issues in Sidecar.vacuum()'s measure() helper: (1) measures page_count*page_size, not actual file size, so deleted-but-not-returned-to-OS pages report 0 saved even when the file shrinks; (2) VACUUM is a no-op on :memory: databases, so tests using an in-memory sidecar would always show before===after; (3) two separate PRAGMA prepare calls per measure() invocation is wasteful and has minor TOCTOU exposure on page_size across the two calls. All low severity, none blocking; deferred as follow-up rather than scope-creeping the retention/rotation PR.
notes: Ref: PR #58 review threads, comments 3755059147, 3755059155, 3755059185.
